Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life.

Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life.

sub_query_2.chapter_title: OF OFFENCES AGAINST WOMAN AND CHILD
sub_query_2.text: Whoever kidnaps or abducts any woman with intent that she may be compelled, or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled, to marry any person against her will, or in order that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, or knowing it to be likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and whoever, by means of criminal intimidation as defined in this Sanhita or of abuse of authority or any other method of compulsion, induces any woman to go from any place with intent that she may be, or knowing that it is likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person shall also be punishable as aforesaid. Of causing miscarriage, etc. Causing miscarriage. [OF CAUSING MISCARRIAGE, ETC.]

phase11.detailed_answer: The relevant offence for obstructing a public road and causing danger is outlined in Section 285 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. This section states that anyone who causes danger, obstruction, or injury to any person in a public way through their actions or negligence can be punished with a fine of up to five thousand rupees. Additionally, Section 270 defines a public nuisance as any act or omission that causes common injury, danger, or annoyance to the public, which may also apply in this context. Furthermore, Section 281 addresses reckless or negligent driving on public ways, which could also be relevant if the obstruction involved a vehicle.
